title: Microsoft Edge: expanded enforcement controls for Data Loss Prevention connectors
summary: Hold: the briefing treats the planned controls as admin-opt-in without evidence of their default, and promises a bypass audit trail and justification reporting that Microsoft has not documented. It also labels connector automation as undocumented despite existing policies, asserts separate licensing without support, and links several policy names to references that document only one of them.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[2].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not yet explain the planned expansion or how its justification control relates to the existing field.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge DLP connectors expanded enforcement download required bypass justification administrator defined guidance default licensing; opened DLP overview, Symantec setup and all three connector policy references. Found existing controls, not an explanation of the planned expansion.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The new controls are admin-opt-in and nothing changes if administrators do nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge DLP connectors expanded enforcement download required bypass justification administrator defined guidance default licensing; Edge connectors 579894 default. Read roadmap, connector overview and Symantec setup; no new-control arrival default stated.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Replace 'If nobody acts, nothing changes' with 'Existing connectors require configuration; Microsoft has not stated defaults for the new controls or their effect on existing configurations.' Update the risk rationale to assess today's behaviour continuing, without asserting an opt-in default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing and pricing specifically for the new controls are not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge DLP connectors license Symantec Trellix Cisco Secure Access licensing cost; expanded enforcement download required bypass justification administrator defined guidance default licensing. Read security connectors overview and Symantec setup; no new-control licence or price found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The security connectors overview says existing connectors extend security investments at no additional cost.
claims.quote: These connectors allow Edge for Business to align with your established security protocols, extending the reach of your security investments at no additional cost.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each third-party DLP product has its own licence and is a separate cost.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge DLP connectors license Symantec Trellix Cisco Secure Access licensing cost; Edge DLP connectors license Symantec. Read Symantec setup, connectors overview and Trellix/Cisco search excerpts; product dependencies are described, not a separate licence or charge for each.
claims.fix: Replace the separate-licence and separate-cost assertions with 'The connectors integrate with third-party security products; Microsoft Learn does not specify their licensing or charges here. Confirm vendor entitlements separately.' Keep the new-controls licensing model unknown.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Enabled DLP connectors send content from specified user actions to an on-device DLP agent.
claims.quote: When enabled, Microsoft Edge sends content from specific user actions to the on-device agent and waits for the verdict before proceeding.

claims.claim: The existing connector waits for a verdict, with waiting configurable per browser action.
claims.quote: If set to 1, Microsoft Edge waits for a response from the analysis service before giving the page access to the data. Any other integer value allows the page to access the data immediately.

claims.quote: Each configuration policy can be assigned to multiple Microsoft Entra groups, and a group can be assigned to multiple configuration policies.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Administrators can review bypass justifications through the DLP provider console and Edge reporting connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Edge DLP connectors bypass justification reporting logs reporting connector console; Edge DLP justification reporting connector. claims.fix: Remove the instruction to review justifications through those consoles. Retain the Open questions item about where justifications are recorded and whether administrators can read them; recommend validating reporting support with the provider before relying on it.

claims.claim: Edge reporting connectors can report DLP-related browser events.
claims.quote: Sensitive data transfer | Content marked as sensitive by DLP scan (requires Analysis connector to be configured).

Do not equate these events with justification reporting.
